mainTopic: What the lists of damage categories of the משנה, רבי אושעיא and רבי חייא include and leave out, and the משנה's comparisons between the אבות
overview: The גמרא keeps asking why certain payments are missing from רבי אושעיא's list of damage categories. עדים זוממין are left off because he follows רבי עקיבא, for whom their payment is a קנס. An ox that hurts a person is not split off, because even רבי עקיבא says it is paid only from the ox's body. The אונס, מפתה and מוציא שם רע, and the מטמא, מדמע and מנסך, are each either already covered by an existing category or are a קנס, which the list does not include. The גמרא then asks what רבי חייא's number of twenty-four leaves out. It answers the מפגל, because the list does not deal with קדשים, and the מוסר, because his damage is only through speech. The מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין stay on the list, because one's speech comes with an action and the other's speech is called an action by the תורה. רבי אבהו explains that 'אבות' in the long lists means everything is paid from מיטב, learned from four shared words. Finally the גמרא begins explaining the משנה's comparisons between שור, מבעה and the living categories, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why are conspiring witnesses left off the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why עדים זוממין, whose payment is a money payment, are not included in רבי אושעיא's list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conspiring witnesses pay money. So they should be listed too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list of damage categories. עדים זוממין pay money for the loss they tried to cause, so why are they not counted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list seems to include every case where a person must pay ממון for harm. עדים זוממין pay the exact amount they tried to make someone lose, which looks like ממון. So leaving them out looks like a gap in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven to have lied, who must pay what they tried to cause
A money payment that makes up a real loss (not a fine)
Let him teach it (why is it not on the list?)

phrases.english: Conspiring witnesses,
which is a money payment, let him teach it!
phrases.notes: The 'him' is רבי אושעיא, whose ברייתא lists the categories of damage.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's list of damage categories
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עדים זוממין pay ממון, so by the list's own standard they should be included.

steps.title: He follows רבי עקיבא: their payment is a fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא, who says עדים זוממין do not pay if they admit on their own, which shows their payment is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי עקיבא, who says they do not pay based on their own admission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא. In his view the payment of עדים זוממין is a fine, so it does not belong on a list of money payments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real money debt is paid even if a person admits it himself. A קנס is paid only when witnesses prove it, not by admission. Since רבי עקיבא says עדים זוממין do not pay by their own admission, their payment must be a קנס, so it is left off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (follows the view of)
They do not pay based on their own admission
A fine, which is not paid if one admits on his own

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic test: a payment you owe even when you admit it is ממון, and one you owe only through witnesses is קנס.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין עַל פִּי עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: who says: they do not pay based on their own admission.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the list to a specific opinion (רבי עקיבא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The payment of עדים זוממין is ממון and should be listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא it is a קנס, so it does not belong on a list of ממון payments.

steps.title: Then he should list two kinds of ox
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא, he should list an ox that damages property and an ox that injures a person as two separate categories.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds like רבי עקיבא, let him teach two kinds of ox: an ox that damages an ox, and an ox that damages a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around and challenges it. If רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא, he should also follow him on another point and split שור into two categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying he follows רבי עקיבא now causes a new problem. רבי עקיבא treats an ox that hurts a person differently from an ox that damages property. So the list should show them as two separate categories, but it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: If he holds (this view)
Two types
That damages

phrases.english: If he holds like Rabbi Akiva,
let him teach two types of ox:
let him teach an ox that damages an ox,
and let him teach an ox that damages a person;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לִיתְנֵי תְּרֵי גַוְונֵי שׁוֹר
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 2 that רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he follows רבי עקיבא, he should list every distinction רבי עקיבא makes, including two kinds of שור.

steps.title: Source: רבי עקיבא says a תם that hurts a person pays full damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי עקיבא says a שור תם that injured a person pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי עקיבא says, even a תם that injured a person pays full damage for the difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its challenge. It shows that רבי עקיבא really treats an ox that hurts a person differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a שור תם (an ox not known to gore) pays only half damage. רבי עקיבא says that when it hurts a person, the owner pays full damage. This different payment is why the ox that hurts a person would seem to deserve its own category.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
An ox not known to gore, which usually pays half damage
Full damage
The difference (the extra amount)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תם and מועד: a תם normally pays only half. The surprise here is that רבי עקיבא makes a תם pay full damage when it hurts a person.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Akiva says:
even an innocuous ox that injured a person
pays full damage for the difference!
phrases.notes: This comes from a case where the ox and the person hurt each other, so the owner pays the extra amount his ox caused.

steps.raayaObject: The challenge that רבי עקיבא treats an ox that hurts a person as different
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה: רבי עקיבא says a תם that injured a person pays full damage

steps.title: רבי עקיבא himself weakened that ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא limits his own ruling: a תם that hurts a person is paid only from the ox's body, not from the owner's best property, so it is not a main category.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי עקיבא broke the force of his own ruling. As it was taught, רבי עקיבא says: You might think even a תם that injured a person pays from the best property. So the verse says 'shall be done to him': he pays from its body, and not from the best property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא himself limited his ruling. Even for him, the owner pays only from the ox itself, so this case does not count as a separate main category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main categories on the list are paid from the owner's best property (עלייה). רבי עקיבא learns from 'יעשה לו' that a תם that hurt a person is paid only from the ox's body. Since it does not meet that standard, the list has no reason to give it its own category.

keyTerms.meaning: He broke his own fist, meaning he weakened his own ruling
As it was taught in a ברייתא
The owner's best property
From its body (the value of the ox itself)
The verse teaches

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא follows רבי עקיבא, so עדים זוממין are a קנס and left off. An ox that hurts a person is not split off either, because even רבי עקיבא says it is paid only from the ox's body.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a main category on the list is one paid from the owner's best property, not just any case with a different payment.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Akiva broke his own fist;
phrases.notes: This is just an expression: he weakened the force of his own ruling.

phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
One might think that even an innocuous ox that injured a person
would pay from the best property;
the verse says: "shall be done to him"
he pays from its body,
and he does not pay from the best property.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the cited ruling is limited by the same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a תם that hurts a person pays full damage for רבי עקיבא, it should be its own category.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי עקיבא says it is paid only from the ox's body, not from the best property, so it is not a main category.

steps.title: Why are the rapist, seducer and defamer missing from the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אושעיא did not list the אונס, the מפתה and the מוציא שם רע, since they all pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rapist, the seducer, and the one who spreads a bad name about a woman all pay money, so רבי אושעיא should list them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to three more cases where a person must pay money. It asks why they are not on רבי אושעיא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that רבי אושעיא lists only real money payments, not fines. The אונס, the מפתה and the מוציא שם רע all have to pay. So if their payments count as money, they seem to belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forces himself on a young unmarried girl
A man who seduces a young unmarried girl
A husband who falsely claims his new wife was not faithful
Let him teach it (he should have listed it)

phrases.english: The rapist, and the seducer, and the defamer,
since it is a money payment, let him teach them!
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אושעיא, whose list we have been discussing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge to the completeness of רבי אושעיא's list, following the same pattern as Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of רבי אושעיא's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The list is supposed to include money payments. These three cases involve money payments, so they should appear on it.

steps.title: Their payments are either already listed or are fines
steps.stepSummary: Each part of their payment is either נזק, צער or בושת, which are already listed (פגם counts as נזק), or it is a קנס, which רבי אושעיא does not discuss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if it is for damage, he listed it. If for pain, he listed it. If for shame, he listed it. If for lowering her value, that is the same as damage. What is left to say? The fine? He does not talk about fines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these cases do not need their own spot. Every part of the payment is either already on the list or is a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the payment into its pieces. נזק, צער and בושת are already categories on the list, and פגם is really just a kind of נזק. The only piece left is the fixed fine the תורה sets, and Step 2 already showed that רבי אושעיא does not list fines.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it (both options lead to the same answer)
Payment for pain
Payment for embarrassment or humiliation
Loss of value or status
A fine: a set amount, not based on the actual loss

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think these cases are not real payments at all. The point is that every part of the payment is either already covered by another category or is a קנס. So they don't need a new category on this list.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
if it is for damage, he already taught it;
if it is for pain, he already taught it;
if it is for humiliation, he already taught it;
if it is for degradation, that is the same as damage.
What else do you have to say? The fine?
phrases.notes: He means the fixed amount the תורה makes these men pay, no matter what the real loss is.

phrases.english: He does not speak about fines.
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 2: רבי אושעיא's list does not include fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Either way: each part of the payment is already covered or falls outside the list's scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These cases pay money, so they need their own category.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their payments are either already covered by נזק, צער or בושת, or they are a קנס, which the list does not include.

steps.title: Why are the one who makes impure, mixes, or pours to idols missing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the מטמא, the מדמע and the מנסך are not on the list, since they also pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who makes someone's food impure, the one who mixes תרומה into someone's food, and the one who pours someone's wine to an idol all pay money, so he should list them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new group of cases where a person must pay money. It asks again why they are not on רבי אושעיא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases the object looks exactly the same as before. But its halachic status has changed, so it is now worth less to the owner. Since the one who did this pays money, it seems he should be a category on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes another person's pure food (like תרומה) impure
One who mixes תרומה into another person's regular food, so it may no longer be eaten by just anyone
One who pours another person's wine as an offering to an idol, making it forbidden
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: One who makes impure, and one who mixes, and one who pours as a libation,
phrases.notes: All three ruin someone else's food or wine by changing its halachic status, not its look or taste.

phrases.english: since it is a money payment, let him teach them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge in the same pattern as Step 6, using a different group of cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of רבי אושעיא's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These people cause a loss that must be paid with money, so they should have their own category.

steps.title: Hidden damage is either regular damage or a fine
steps.stepSummary: If a היזק שאינו ניכר counts as damage, it is already covered by נזק. If it does not count as damage, the payment is a קנס, which the list does not include.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if damage you cannot see counts as damage, he already listed damage. If damage you cannot see does not count as damage, then the payment is a fine, and he does not talk about fines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another 'either way' argument. These cases are either already included under נזק or are a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether damage you cannot see, where the object looks unchanged, counts as real damage. If yes, it fits under the נזק already on the list. If no, the payment must be a קנס, and fines are outside this list.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage you cannot see: the object looks the same, but its status has changed
He is speaking about (dealing with)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא's list is complete. Any case left off it is either already included under an existing category, like נזק, or is a קנס, and fines do not belong on his list.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק –
phrases.english: if damage that is not visible is called damage,
then he already taught damage;

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לָא שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק –
phrases.english: if damage that is not visible is not called damage,
then it is a fine,
and he does not speak about fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8, using the same either-way method as Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Either way: depends on whether damage you cannot see counts as damage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These cases pay money, so they need their own category.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either they fall under נזק, which is already listed, or they are a קנס, which is outside the list's scope.

steps.title: Does רבי חייא hold that hidden damage is not real damage?
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי חייא lists the מטמא, מדמע and מנסך as separate categories, the גמרא suggests he holds that a היזק שאינו ניכר is not called damage. Otherwise they would already be covered by נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say רבי חייא holds that damage you cannot see is not called damage. If it were called damage, he already listed נזק, so why list these cases again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests an idea. Maybe רבי חייא's separate listing of these cases shows his view on hidden damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 we learned that if hidden damage counts as damage, it falls under נזק. רבי חייא lists the מטמא, מדמע and מנסך as extra items anyway. So the גמרא suggests he must hold that hidden damage is not damage and that these payments are only a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggested inference.
He holds (in his view)
Damage that cannot be seen. The object looks the same but has lost its value.
It is called damage (it counts legally as damage)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabbi Chiya holds

phrases.aramaic: הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לָא שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק?
phrases.english: that damage that is not visible is not called damage?
For if it were called damage,
he has already taught damage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two-sided logic of Step 9 to רבי חייא's list
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's separate listing of the מטמא, מדמע and מנסך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If hidden damage were damage, these cases would already be included in נזק and listing them would be redundant. So he must hold that it is not damage.

steps.title: Visible and hidden damage are listed separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי חייא may hold that hidden damage is real damage, but he lists visible damage and hidden damage as two separate kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught damage you can see, and he also taught damage you cannot see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from Step 10. Listing hidden damage separately does not prove it is not damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that נזק already includes every kind of damage. The גמרא answers that רבי חייא's נזק means only visible damage. He gives hidden damage its own entries, so nothing is repeated and no conclusion about his view can be drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage that is visible
Damage that is not visible

phrases.english: He taught damage that is visible,
and he taught damage that is not visible.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא הֶיזֵּקָא דְּמִינַּכְרָא, וּתְנָא הֶיזֵּקָא דְּלָא מִינַּכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of Step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof about רבי חייא's view of היזק שאינו ניכר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that נזק in his list covers all damage. It may cover only visible damage.

steps.title: What does רבי חייא's number come to leave out?
steps.stepSummary: Each list opens with a number. The משנה's 'four' leaves out רבי אושעיא's extra items, and רבי אושעיא's 'thirteen' leaves out רבי חייא's extra items. But what does רבי חייא's 'twenty-four' leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that our משנה gave a number to leave out רבי אושעיא's extra categories, and that רבי אושעיא gave a number to leave out רבי חייא's. But רבי חייא's number, what does it leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the numbers placed at the start of each list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A number at the head of a list suggests that the list is closed and that something else is being left out. For the shorter lists, the longer list shows what is left out. רבי חייא has the longest list, so there is no bigger list for his number to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (the next line asks what does not make sense)
Our תנא (the author of our משנה)
The number (the count at the start of the list)
To leave out / to exclude

phrases.english: Granted, according to our tanna,
he taught the number to exclude those of Rabbi Oshaya;
and Rabbi Oshaya taught the number
to exclude those of Rabbi Chiya.
But the number of Rabbi Chiya,
what does it come to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the numbers in the lists
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What category רבי חייא's number of 24 is meant to leave out

steps.title: It leaves out the informer and the one who makes a sacrifice פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's number leaves out the מוסר (an informer who causes someone's property to be taken by the authorities) and the מפגל (a כהן who makes a קרבן invalid through wrong intent).
steps.simpleTranslation: It leaves out the informer and the one who makes a sacrifice פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 12 by naming two cases that cause loss but are not on רבי חייא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the מוסר and the מפגל cause another person a money loss. רבי חייא's number tells us that these two are not among his main categories.

keyTerms.meaning: An informer who hands over another person's money or property to the authorities
Someone who makes a קרבן פיגול (invalid) through improper intent during the service

phrases.english: To exclude an informer and one who renders an offering piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number leaves out the מוסר and the מפגל

steps.title: Why not list the informer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי חייא does not list these cases. It accepts that the מפגל is left out because רבי חייא does not deal with קדשים, but the מוסר still needs a reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him list them! The מפגל makes sense, since he does not deal with holy items. But the informer, why did he not list him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 13. If these cases cause loss, why are they not on the list? It then narrows the challenge to the מוסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מפגל is easy to explain, because רבי חייא's list is only about ordinary property and not קדשים. The מוסר involves ordinary money, so that reason does not work for him, and the question now focuses on the מוסר alone. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach it! (why not include it?)
Holy items, such as קרבנות
He is not dealing with (this topic)

phrases.english: Then let him teach them!
Granted the one who renders piggul: he does not deal with consecrated items.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מוֹסֵר, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי?
phrases.english: But the informer, what is the reason he did not teach it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leaving out of the cases named in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the מוסר is left off רבי חייא's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מוסר causes loss of ordinary money, so the reason about קדשים that explains the מפגל does not apply to him.

steps.title: The informer damages only through speech
steps.stepSummary: The מוסר is different because he causes damage only by speaking, and רבי חייא's list does not deal with damage done through speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: The informer is different, because his damage comes through speech, and רבי חייא does not deal with damage done through speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the מוסר: his damage comes only through speech. The next steps test this answer against the מוציא שם רע and עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item on רבי חייא's list involves some physical action or a thing that does damage. The מוסר only talks, and the authorities do the actual taking. So he falls outside the type of damage the list covers. This does not mean he is free of liability; he is simply not part of this list.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Speech

steps.whatToRemember: The number at the head of each list leaves something out. The משנה's four leaves out רבי אושעיא's extras, and רבי אושעיא's thirteen leaves out רבי חייא's extras. רבי חייא's twenty-four leaves out the מפגל (קדשים) and the מוסר (damage through speech).
steps.confusionAlert: Leaving the מוסר off this list does not mean he never pays. It only means damage through speech is not one of the main categories רבי חייא is listing.

phrases.english: An informer is different, since it is through speech,
and with speech he does not deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the list to damage done by action, not speech
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מוסר causes a real money loss, so he should be listed
steps.terutzMaskana: The list covers only damage done by action, and the מוסר damages only through speech

steps.title: Challenge: The defamer damages through speech, yet he is listed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer: the מוציא שם רע causes damage through speech, yet רבי חייא lists him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the defamer causes damage through speech, and רבי חייא still lists him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 15. If רבי חייא leaves out damage done through speech, why does he include the מוציא שם רע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the מוסר is missing because his damage comes only from talking. But the מוציא שם רע also harms through words, and he is in רבי חייא's list. So the rule 'no speech cases' seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who falsely says his wife was not faithful before the marriage
Speech, talking
And yet he teaches it (it is in his list)

phrases.english: But isn't there the defamer,
whose damage is through speech, and yet he teaches it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, דְּדִיבּוּרָא הוּא, וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי חייא's list leaves out damage done through speech
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case in the list (מוציא שם רע) is also damage through speech, so the rule seems broken

steps.title: Answer: The defamer's speech comes with an action
steps.stepSummary: The מוציא שם רע is different because his speech is joined to an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speech that has an action connected to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מוציא שם רע is not pure talk. His case also involves something he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 15 is made sharper: רבי חייא leaves out damage done through speech alone. The מוסר only talks, but the מוציא שם רע's speech comes with an action, so he fits in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: That has an action in it

phrases.english: It is speech that involves an action.
phrases.notes: The action is that he is only liable if he makes his claim after living with her as husband and wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: speech with an action versus speech alone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מוציא שם רע seemed to be a pure speech case like the מוסר
steps.terutzMaskana: His speech is joined to an action, so only pure speech cases are left out

steps.title: Challenge: Plotting witnesses use speech with no action, yet they are listed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: עדים זוממין harm only through speech with no action, yet רבי חייא lists them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But עדים זוממין are speech with no action at all, and he still lists them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes harder against the sharper rule from Step 17. עדים זוממין only testify, so their case is pure speech, and they are still in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about an 'action' does not help here. The witnesses only spoke in court and did nothing physical. So again a pure speech case seems to be in רבי חייא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven to have lied, who get the punishment they tried to bring on someone else
That has no action in it

phrases.english: But isn't there the case of plotting witnesses –
which is speech that involves no action,
and yet he teaches it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין דִּיבּוּרָא דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא, וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sharper rule given in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that רבי חייא leaves out speech with no action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עדים זוממין are pure speech with no action, yet they are listed

steps.title: Answer: The תורה calls the plotting witnesses' speech an action
steps.stepSummary: Even though עדים זוממין do no action, the תורה describes what they did as an action, using the word 'do.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, even though there is no action, the תורה calls it an action, as it says: 'And you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עדים זוממין are a special case. The פסוק itself treats their plotting as 'doing,' so they count as an action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Physically, the witnesses only spoke. But the פסוק says 'as he plotted to do,' describing their words as doing. Because the תורה calls it an action, it fits in רבי חייא's list, while the מוסר stays out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Calls it
Plotted, planned

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא's list leaves out damage done through speech alone. The מוציא שם רע is in because his speech comes with an action, and עדים זוממין are in because the תורה calls their speech an action.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: There, even though it involves no action,
the Merciful One calls it an action –
as it is written: "And you shall do to him
as he plotted to do to his brother."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה, רַחֲמָנָא קַרְיֵיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק defines the case as an action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עדים זוממין seemed to be pure speech, like the מוסר
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה calls their plotting an action, so they belong in the list

steps.title: Challenge: If רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא list everything, what are their תולדות?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אבות' makes sense in our משנה, which leaves room for תולדות. But רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא also say 'אבות' and seem to list everything, so what are their תולדות?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the תנא of our משנה, who says 'אבות,' which shows there are תולדות. But רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא also say 'אבות,' which should show there are תולדות. What are their תולדות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the word 'אבות.' It asks what 'subcategories' could be left over in the long lists of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling something an 'אב' (main category) suggests there are also 'תולדות' (offshoots) under it. In our משנה's short list that is easy to understand. But the longer lists seem to include all the kinds of damage, so the word 'אבות' looks out of place there.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (opens a 'this is fine, but that is hard' question)
Main categories
Subcategories, offshoots of the main categories
By implication, which shows that

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the tanna of our Mishnah,
he taught "main categories" –
which implies that there are subcategories;
but according to Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Oshaya,
"main categories" – does that imply there are subcategories?!
What are their subcategories?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְתַנָּא דִּידַן, תַּנָּא אָבוֹת מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא תּוֹלְדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the speech question and opens a new question about the word 'אבות'
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the word 'אבות' by רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אבות' suggests that there are תולדות, but their lists seem to leave nothing over to be תולדות

steps.title: רבי אבהו: All of them are like אבות in paying from the best property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that 'אבות' in these lists means that all the items are paid like אבות, from the best-quality property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: All of them are like אבות, in that one pays from the best property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question about the word 'אבות.' Here the word does not point to תולדות. It tells us how these damages are paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אבות' is understood in a new way. It does not mean 'main categories that have offshoots.' It means 'treated like the אבות,' so payment for all these damages comes from מיטב, the best-quality property.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the main categories, treated the same way
The best-quality property
To pay

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אבות' does not mean 'main categories with subcategories under them.' For רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא it means these damages are paid like the אבות, from the best property.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבהו, 'אבות' in the lists of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא means that every item is paid from מיטב, just like the main אבות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
All of them are like main categories
in that one must pay from the best-quality property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: כּוּלָּן כְּאָבוֹת לְשַׁלֵּם מִמֵּיטַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אבות' means main categories that have תולדות under them
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, 'אבות' means all are paid from מיטב, like the main אבות

steps.title: What is the source for paying from the best land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that all the damages in רבי חייא's list are paid from the best-quality property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אבהו's rule from the last step. This question sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said that every item in the list is paid like an אב, from עידית (the best land). The תורה says this openly only for a few damages, so the גמרא wants to know how it spreads to all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Here it means: what is the source?
The best-quality land or property, which is what damages are paid from

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that all the listed damages are paid from the best-quality property

steps.title: Four shared words carry the rule to every damage
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned through a גזירה שוה from the words 'תחת', 'נתינה', 'ישלם' and 'כסף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the words 'in place of,' 'giving,' 'he shall pay,' and 'money.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from four words in the damage פסוקים. Each damage in the list is described with at least one of these words, so the rule about the best land carries over to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוקים where these words appear, the rule of paying from the best property is clear. Every other damage in the list uses one of the same words. Through a גזירה שוה, it is linked to those פסוקים and gets the same payment rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned from
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both places
'In place of,' said about a שור מועד that gores
'He shall pay'

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why every item in the long lists of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא can be called an 'אב': each one is paid from מיטב, just like the main אבות.

phrases.english: It is learned from 'in place of,' 'giving,'
phrases.notes: These words come from שמות 21:36 and שמות 21:32.

phrases.english: 'he shall pay,' 'money.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the four words תחת, נתינה, ישלם and כסף carries the best-property payment rule to every listed damage

steps.title: What does 'שור is not like מבעה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line comparing שור and מבעה and asks what it is trying to say.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The case of the Ox is not like the case of the מבעה.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its next line. It asks what the comparison between שור and מבעה is meant to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that these two categories are different. It does not say why that difference matters. The גמרא wants to know the point of the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The case of one is not like the case of the other'
One of the four אבות נזיקין in the משנה
What is he saying? A request to explain the meaning

phrases.english: The case of the Ox is not like the case of the Maveh.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הֲרֵי הַשּׁוֹר כַּהֲרֵי הַמַּבְעֶה. מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to explain its next phrase
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and purpose of the משנה's comparison between שור and מבעה

steps.title: One category cannot be learned from another
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד in the name of רבא explains that the משנה first suggests writing only one category, then rejects this because each one is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: This is what it means. Let the תורה write one category and learn the other from it. Then the משנה says: one cannot be learned from the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד explains that the משנה is asking why the תורה needed to write each category. The משנה's answer is that each category has its own special features, so one could not be learned from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line in the משנה is a short way of saying 'maybe write only one.' It then answers 'no, they are different.' Because of these differences, each אב needed its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One,' meaning the תורה or ה׳
And let it be learned
Then he says, a turn to the conclusion
One from one

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean that one category is less real than another. It only means that each one has its own features, so the תורה had to write each one separately.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
This is what it is saying:
Let the Merciful One write one,
and the other will be learned from it;
then it says:
one cannot be learned from one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה suggests learning one category from another and rejects it, because each category is different

steps.title: What does 'living spirit' in the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next line, about categories that have a living spirit, asks what it means, and רב משרשיא in the name of רבא begins to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not this and that, which have a living spirit.' What is it saying? רב משרשיא said in the name of רבא: This is what it means:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks what it means. Then it starts רב משרשיא's explanation, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה groups שור and מבעה together because both are alive. It sets them against something that is not alive. The גמרא needs to explain what this comparison teaches, and רבא's explanation is only being introduced here.

keyTerms.meaning: A living spirit, meaning a living creature
This one and that one, meaning both of them together

phrases.english: And not this and that,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means שור and מבעה together.

phrases.english: which have a living spirit.
What is it saying?
Rav Mesharshiya said in the name of Rava:
This is what it is saying:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא זֶה וָזֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן רוּחַ חַיִּים. מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the משנה's next comparison, following the same pattern as step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the משנה's line grouping the living categories together against a category that is not alive
